Acromegaly/Gigantism: Caused by chronic excess of Growth Hormone (GH), usually from a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma.

snip.t: When GH oversecretion occurs before epiphyseal closure in children, it leads to Gigantism, characterized by excessive linear growth.

snip.t: Excess GH after epiphyseal closure causes acromegaly; gigantism (A) occurs only if excess GH begins before growth plate closure (childhood).

snip.t: Clinical Relevance: Excess GH before epiphyseal plate closure leads to gigantism; after closure, it leads to acromegaly.

snip.t: Hallmark: Gigantism of both the cytoplasm and nucleus of infected cells, with a large intranuclear inclusion surrounded by a clear halo, often described as an "owl's eye" inclusion.
